mainTopic: Why the תורה writes שליחות יד for both the שומר חנם and the שומר שכר, and what each mention teaches
overview: רבי יוחנן finishes his statement by saying that the שליחות יד written for a שומר שכר is not 'different.' The 'different' view says a קל וחומר from a שומר חנם already teaches the שומר שכר's liability, so his פסוק must teach something new: שליחות יד does not need a loss. רבי יוחנן follows רבי אלעזר, who says both cases are the same. The קל וחומר can be challenged because a שומר חנם pays double when he falsely claims a thief took the item. The other side answers that paying the principal without an oath is stricter than paying double after an oath. רבא offers a different קל וחומר, from a שואל, which would make both mentions of שליחות יד look extra. He explains that one mention teaches that no loss is needed, and the other blocks the rule of דיו, so a שומר is liable even when the owner is working with him. According to the view that a loss is required, one mention blocks דיו, and the other is used by a ברייתא to show that 'approaching the judges' means taking an oath.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: It Is Not Different
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן finishes his statement by giving his own view: the שליחות יד written about a שומר שכר is not special.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I say: it is not different.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן finishes his statement. The view he just quoted called the שומר שכר's שליחות יד 'different,' but his own opinion is that it is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this line, רבי יוחנן quoted a view that the שליחות יד said about a שומר שכר is 'different,' meaning it teaches a special rule. Here he disagrees. The גמרא will now explain both sides.

keyTerms.meaning: A guardian using or taking the item he was given to watch for himself
Different, special, teaching an unusual rule
It is not different

phrases.english: And I say: it is not different.
phrases.notes: 'It' means the שליחות יד that the תורה writes about a שומר שכר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יוחנן's statement from before this section by giving his own disagreeing view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי יוחנן's own view, the שליחות יד written about a שומר שכר does not teach any special rule.

steps.title: What Does 'Different' Mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the first view meant when it called the שומר שכר's שליחות יד 'different.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an explanation of the word 'different.' This question sets up the next steps, which explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We cannot judge רבי יוחנן's disagreement until we know what the other side means. So the גמרא first explains the 'different' view.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is...? (asking for an explanation)

phrases.english: And what is 'different'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the view that רבי יוחנן just rejected actually means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what way is the שליחות יד written about a שומר שכר 'different'?

steps.title: A קל וחומר Would Have Been Enough
steps.stepSummary: The 'different' view: we did not need a פסוק for a שומר שכר, because a קל וחומר from a שומר חנם already teaches it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let שליחות יד not be written about a שומר שכר, and learn it from a שומר חנם. If a שומר חנם, who is exempt for theft and loss, is liable when he does שליחות יד, then surely a שומר שכר, who is liable for theft and loss, is liable too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the 'different' view. A שומר שכר's liability for שליחות יד could have been learned with a קל וחומר, so writing it in the תורה looks unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומר חנם is the more lenient guardian, since he does not pay for theft or loss. A שומר שכר is stricter, since he does pay for theft or loss. If even the lenient guardian pays for שליחות יד, the strict one certainly does, so the פסוק about the שומר שכר seems to be extra.

keyTerms.meaning: A paid guardian
An unpaid guardian
Theft and loss
All the more so (the conclusion of a קל וחומר)
And let it come (be learned) from...

phrases.aramaic: לֹא תֵּאָמֵר שְׁלִיחוּת יָד בְּשׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר,
phrases.english: Let misappropriation not be stated about a paid guardian,
and learn it from an unpaid guardian:
If an unpaid guardian,
who is exempt for theft and loss,
is liable if he misappropriated it,
then a paid guardian, who is liable for theft and loss,
is he not liable all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא תֵּאָמֵר שְׁלִיחוּת יָד בְּשׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering what 'different' means by showing that the פסוק looks extra.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק about the שומר שכר seems unnecessary, because a קל וחומר from a שומר חנם could teach it.

steps.title: The Extra פסוק: No Loss Needed
steps.stepSummary: Since the פסוק is extra, it teaches a new rule: שליחות יד makes a guardian liable even without any actual loss to the item.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law did the תורה write it? To tell you: שליחות יד does not need loss.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining the 'different' view. The extra פסוק teaches that a guardian becomes liable for שליחות יד even if the item was not damaged or reduced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a פסוק is not needed for its simple meaning, we use it to teach something new. Here the new lesson is that שליחות יד does not need חסרון. That is why this view calls the פסוק 'different.'

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? (what does it come to teach?)
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה or ה׳
Loss, a reduction in the item

steps.whatToRemember: The 'different' view: a קל וחומר already teaches the שומר שכר's liability, so his פסוק is free to teach that שליחות יד does not need חסרון.

phrases.english: For what law did the Merciful One write it?
To tell you:
Misappropriation does not require loss.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the extra פסוק shown in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra פסוק teaches that שליחות יד does not need חסרון. That is what makes it 'different.'

steps.title: רבי יוחנן Follows רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says his view, that it is not different, follows רבי אלעזר, who said both cases are one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I say it is not different, like רבי אלעזר, who said: this and that are one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back רבי יוחנן's view and shows that it follows רבי אלעזר. רבי אלעזר said the שומר חנם case and the שומר שכר case are 'one.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the two cases are 'one' means the שומר שכר פסוק does not teach any special extra lesson. The meaning of 'one' is still unclear, so the גמרא will ask about it next.

keyTerms.meaning: This and that are one (both cases are the same)

steps.confusionAlert: This line repeats the words of step 1 on purpose. The גמרא is now giving the reason and source for רבי יוחנן's view.

phrases.english: And I say: it is not different,
in line with רבי אלעזר, who said:
This and that are one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲנִי אוֹמֵר: אֵינָהּ מְשׁוּנָּה כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי יוחנן's opinion from step 1 after the 'different' view was explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Following רבי אלעזר, the שליחות יד of the שומר חנם and of the שומר שכר are the same, and the שומר שכר פסוק teaches nothing special.

steps.title: What Does 'This and That Are One' Mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי אלעזר meant by 'this and that are one.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'this and that are one'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what 'one' means. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק is not teaching a new rule, the גמרא must explain why the תורה wrote it at all. The answer must show that the קל וחומר from step 3 fails.

keyTerms.meaning: What is...? / What does it mean?

phrases.english: What is 'this and that are one'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an explanation of רבי אלעזר's phrase from step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what way are the two cases 'one,' and why is the שומר שכר פסוק needed?

steps.title: The קל וחומר Can Be Challenged
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר fails, because a שומר חנם is stricter in one way: he pays double when he falsely claims a thief took the item.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it can be challenged: what about a שומר חנם? He is different, because he pays double payment when he claims a thief took it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי אלעזר. The קל וחומר from step 3 can be broken, so both פסוקים are needed and neither one is extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר works only if one side is stricter in every way. A שומר חנם who falsely claims a thief took the item pays תשלומי כפל, and a שומר שכר does not. Since the שומר חנם is stricter in this way, the קל וחומר fails, and the שומר שכר needs his own פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: It can be refuted (the קל וחומר can be challenged)
What about...? It is different, because... (the formula for breaking a קל וחומר)
Double payment
The claim that a thief stole the item

phrases.english: Because it can be challenged:
What about an unpaid guardian?
He is different, because he pays double payment
when he claims a thief stole it.
phrases.notes: This means a false claim. The guardian really has the item himself but says a thief took it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by breaking the קל וחומר from step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two cases are 'one' because the קל וחומר fails. A שומר חנם is stricter in paying double for a false claim of theft, so both פסוקים are needed.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's view: a קל וחומר cannot teach the שומר שכר's liability, so his פסוק is needed for the basic rule and is not 'different.'

steps.title: Why the Other Side Keeps the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The 'different' view does not accept the challenge. In its view, paying the principal without an oath is stricter than paying double only after an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who does not challenge it holds: paying the principal without an oath is stricter than paying double with an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the 'different' view is not bothered by the challenge in step 7. It holds that the שומר שכר is still the stricter guardian.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומר שכר pays the full value for theft right away, without any oath. A שומר חנם pays double only after he swears falsely. This view counts the שומר שכר's payment as stricter, so the קל וחומר still works and the שומר שכר פסוק stays extra.

keyTerms.meaning: And the one who does not challenge it
The principal, the basic value of the item
An oath
Is greater, more severe
Double payment

steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument depends on one question: is paying the principal without an oath stricter than paying double after an oath? The answer decides whether the קל וחומר works and whether the פסוק is 'different.'
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the whole disagreement comes down to how to compare two kinds of strictness. That decides whether שליחות יד needs חסרון.

phrases.english: And the one who does not challenge it holds:
The principal without an oath
is stricter than double payment with an oath.
phrases.notes: A שומר שכר pays the principal for theft without any oath. A שומר חנם pays double only after swearing falsely.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the 'different' view from steps 3 and 4 against the challenge in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the challenge by comparing which guardian is stricter in a different way
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because a שומר חנם pays double for a false claim of theft, he seems stricter, so the קל וחומר seems to fail.
steps.terutzMaskana: Paying the principal without an oath is stricter than paying double after an oath. So the שומר שכר is stricter overall, and the קל וחומר still works.

steps.title: רבא: The law could have come from a borrower
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the תורה did not need to write שליחות יד for a שומר חנם or a שומר שכר. It could have been learned through a קל וחומר from a שואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: The פסוק should not need to mention misappropriation for an unpaid guardian or a paid guardian. We could learn it from a borrower. A borrower is allowed to use the item, since the owner agreed. Yet if he misappropriates it, he is liable. Then an unpaid or paid guardian, who may not use it at all, should certainly be liable!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא points out that the two mentions of שליחות יד look unnecessary, because we could learn them from a שואל. This sets up his question of why the תורה wrote them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שואל is allowed to use the item, and he is still liable if he misuses it. A שומר is not allowed to use it at all, so he should certainly be liable. That makes the פסוקים for the שומרים look extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Misappropriation: a guardian taking the item for his own use
An unpaid guardian
A paid guardian
A borrower, who may use the item for free
All the more so

phrases.english: Rava says:
Misappropriation should not need to be stated

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בְּשׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם וְלֹא בְּשׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר,
phrases.english: neither for an unpaid guardian nor for a paid guardian,
and let it be learned from a borrower.
Just as a borrower,
who uses the item with the owner's permission,
is liable if he misappropriated it,

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם וְשׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן.
phrases.english: then an unpaid guardian and a paid guardian, all the more so!

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: לֹא תֵּאָמֵר שְׁלִיחוּת יָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the earlier back-and-forth over the קל וחומר, רבא offers a different קל וחומר, this time from a שואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The liability of שומרים for שליחות יד could be learned through a קל וחומר from a שואל.

steps.title: So why does the תורה mention it?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks why the תורה wrote שליחות יד for the שומרים if it could be learned anyway.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks the obvious question that follows from his קל וחומר. He is setting up his own answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the תורה must teach something. If the law could be learned from a שואל, the two mentions must each be teaching something new.

keyTerms.meaning: Why was it stated? (asked about an extra-looking פסוק)

phrases.english: Why, then, was it stated?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows directly from רבא's claim that the פסוקים are not needed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What do the two extra mentions of שליחות יד teach?

steps.title: One mention: no loss needed. The other: blocks דיו
steps.stepSummary: One mention teaches that שליחות יד needs no loss. The other prevents us from applying דיו, which would have exempted a שומר when the owner is with him, just like a שואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: One mention tells you that misappropriation does not need a loss. The other is so you will not say: 'Whatever is learned from a קל וחומר can be no stronger than its source.' Then you would say: just as a borrower is exempt when the owner is with him, so too an unpaid and paid guardian are exempt when the owner is with them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own question by giving each extra mention its own job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of דיו says a law learned through a קל וחומר cannot be stronger than its source. A שואל is exempt when the owner is working with him, so a שומר would be exempt then too. The second mention in the תורה tells us the שומר is liable even in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: A loss or reduction in the item

keyTerms.term: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן
keyTerms.meaning: A law learned through a קל וחומר is no stronger than its source
When the owner is with him, working for him at the time
Exempt

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'בבעלים' does not mean 'with the owner's permission.' It means the owner was working for the borrower or guardian at the time, which is a special case where a שואל is exempt.

phrases.english: One mention is to tell you:
misappropriation does not require a loss.
And the other is so that you will not say,

phrases.aramaic: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כְּנִידּוֹן.
phrases.english: 'It is enough for what is learned from a קל וחומר to be like its source.'
Just as a borrower whose owner is with him is exempt,
phrases.notes: The owner is working for the borrower at the time.

phrases.aramaic: אַף שׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם וְשׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר בִּבְעָלִים פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: so too an unpaid guardian and a paid guardian whose owner is with them are exempt.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One mention teaches that שליחות יד needs no loss. The other cancels the limit of דיו, so a שומר is liable even when the owner is with him.

steps.title: What about the view that a loss is required?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to the view that שליחות יד does need a loss, what are the two mentions for?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says misappropriation requires a loss, why do I need these two mentions of misappropriation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sees that רבא used one mention for 'no loss needed.' It asks how the other view, which requires a loss, explains both mentions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That view cannot use a mention to teach 'no loss needed,' since it disagrees with that rule. So it must find another job for one of the mentions.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
Two
Why do I need it?

phrases.english: And according to the one who says
misappropriation requires a loss,

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי תַּרְתֵּי שְׁלִיחוּת יָד לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: why do I need these two mentions of misappropriation?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר שְׁלִיחוּת יָד צְרִיכָה חֶסְרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבא's approach and asks how the opposing view would explain the extra mentions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What do the two mentions teach according to the view that a loss is required?

steps.title: The first mention still blocks דיו
steps.stepSummary: Even according to this view, one mention is needed to block the rule of דיו.
steps.simpleTranslation: One mention is so that you will not say: 'It is enough for what is learned from a קל וחומר to be like its source.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the first job, which is the same one רבא gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views agree that a mention is needed to stop דיו from exempting a שומר when the owner is with him. The second mention still needs a job, and that comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: One
So that you will not say

phrases.english: One mention is so that you will not say

phrases.aramaic: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן.
phrases.english: 'It is enough for what is learned from a קל וחומר to be like its source.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question from step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One mention cancels the limit of דיו.

steps.title: The second mention is used by a ברייתא about an oath
steps.stepSummary: The other mention is needed for a ברייתא. It teaches that 'the master of the house shall approach the judges' means he must take an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other mention is for what was taught in a ברייתא: 'And the master of the house shall approach the judges.' This means for an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second job and begins quoting a ברייתא that uses this mention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the guardian must come before the judges, but it does not say why. The ברייתא says it is to take an oath, and it will prove this using the extra mention of שליחות יד.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in a ברייתא
The master of the house, meaning the guardian
Here it means the judges
An oath

phrases.english: And the other mention is for what was taught in a ברייתא:
"And the master of the house shall approach the judges"
phrases.notes: שמות 22:7. 'אלהים' here means the judges, not God.

phrases.english: This is for an oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer to step 12 by giving a job to the second mention.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second mention is used to teach that the guardian comes before the judges to swear an oath.

steps.title: The ברייתא asks: oath or judgment?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether 'approach the judges' means for an oath, or only to stand trial.
steps.simpleTranslation: You say it means for an oath. Or maybe it only means for judgment?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own reading. This sets up its proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Coming before judges could simply mean going to court for a ruling. The ברייתא needs a source to show that an oath is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: You say
It is only
Judgment, a court case

phrases.english: You say it is for an oath,
or is it only for judgment?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר לִשְׁבוּעָה, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reading given in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'approach the judges' mean an oath or just a court ruling?

steps.title: Proof: the same words appear by the oath
steps.stepSummary: Both פסוקים use the words שליחות יד. The later one clearly speaks of an oath, so the earlier one does too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Misappropriation is mentioned below, and misappropriation is mentioned above. Just as there it is for an oath, so too here it is for an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves its reading by linking the two פסוקים through their shared words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later פסוק clearly speaks of 'the oath of ה'.' Because the same words שליחות יד appear in both, we learn that the earlier פסוק also means an oath. This is why the view that requires a loss still needs the second mention.

keyTerms.meaning: Below, the later פסוק
Above, the earlier פסוק
There
Learning one פסוק from another through shared words

steps.whatToRemember: In רבא's approach, both views agree that one mention of שליחות יד blocks דיו. The other mention teaches that no loss is needed according to the view that a loss is not required, or is used for the oath גזרה שוה according to the view that a loss is required.

phrases.english: Misappropriation is stated below,
and misappropriation is stated above,
just as there it is for an oath,
so too here it is for an oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question from step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Through a גזרה שוה on the words שליחות יד, the earlier פסוק also refers to an oath.
